candidates.title: CARGO TILT
candidates.description: Tap left or right to route a falling crate onto that dock on a seesaw; dock loads persist and tilt the platform, so a maxed-out side tips and spills while a filled dock ships for bonus score.

candidates.title: MASS SWAP
candidates.description: Tap one drifting orb then a second to instantly swap their positions in the queue heading toward the collector, letting the player reorder which orb (ally or hazard) arrives first.

candidates.title: QUEUE CUT
candidates.description: Tap to open a gate that diverts only the item currently at the gate into its matching color bin; hesitating lets the queue behind it keep advancing and pile up toward overflow.

candidates.title: CHAIN BOND
candidates.description: Tap an orb to select it, then tap a second orb within a short window to bond them into one larger, higher-value orb that can itself be bonded again into an even larger one.

candidates.title: ANCHOR PULL
candidates.description: Drag out from a fixed anchor and release to launch a hook that permanently tethers whatever orb it hits, pulling that orb back whenever it drifts too far; the anchor holds only 2 tethers before the oldest snaps free.

candidates.title: TIDE POOL
candidates.description: Tap a shoreline meter to raise or lower the water level by one notch; each creature is only reachable and tappable at its own specific water level, and the tide keeps drifting on its own.

candidates.title: FUSE LINE
candidates.description: Tap fuse nodes along a branching line to light them in order; a lit node auto-ignites its connected downstream nodes after a delay, but only branches whose upstream junction was already lit will finish before time runs out.

candidates.title: GRID FOLD
candidates.description: Tap a row or column header to shift that entire row or column by one cell with wraparound, sliding tokens around the grid to align matching-colored tokens with a collector token.

candidates.title: BEAM BOUNCE
candidates.description: Drag out a short mirror segment anywhere on the field; a beam fires periodically from a fixed emitter, bounces off any placed mirrors, and must reach a moving receiver before the mirrors are replaced by newer ones.

reason: CARGO TILT scored highest overall (26, tied with MASS SWAP) but led the group on C6: every tap gives an immediate, legible physical response (the seesaw visibly tilts, a fill bar moves, a score popup fires), and unlike MASS SWAP's two-tap selection step or QUEUE CUT's single-lane queue, its persistent dock-load state directly and continuously constrains every later tap's safety, giving it the strongest one-decision-shapes-future-state link (C3) among the top three.
